questions.text: Let $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\mathrm{x}-1}{\mathrm{x}+1}, \mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}-\{0,-1,1)$. If $\mathrm{f}^{n+1}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{f}\left(\mathrm{f}^{\mathrm{n}}(\mathrm{x})\right)$ for all $\mathrm{n} \in \mathrm{N}$, then $\mathrm{f}^{6}(6)+\mathrm{f}^{7}(7)$ is equal to:

options.D:
$-\frac{11}{12}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\mathrm{x}-1}{\mathrm{x}+1}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow f^{2}(x)=f(f(x))=\frac{\frac{x-1}{x+1}-1}{\frac{x-1}{x+1}+1}=-\frac{1}{x} \\
f^{3}(x)=f\left(f^{2}(x)\right)=f\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)=\frac{x+1}{1-x} \\
\Rightarrow f^{4}(x)=f\left(\frac{x+1}{1-x}\right)=-\frac{1}{x} \\
\Rightarrow f^{6}(x)=-\frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow f^{6}(6)=-\frac{1}{8} \\
f^{7}(x)=\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)=\frac{x+1}{1-x} \\
\Rightarrow f^{7}(7)=\frac{8}{-6}=-\frac{4}{3} \\
\therefore-\frac{1}{6}+-\frac{4}{3}=-\frac{3}{2}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\left\{\mathrm{z} \in \mathrm{C}:\left|\frac{\mathrm{z}+1}{\mathrm{z}-1}<1\right|\right\}$
and $\mathrm{B}=\left\{\mathrm{z} \in \mathrm{C}: \arg \left(\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{\mathrm{z}+1}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3}\right\}$.
Then $\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B}$ is :

options.A: a portion of a circle centred at $\left(0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ that lies in the second and third quadrants only
options.B: a portion of a circle centred at $\left(0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ that lies in the second quadrant only
options.D:
a portion of a circle of radius $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ that lies in the third quadrant only

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Set A
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow\left|\frac{\mathrm{z}+1}{\mathrm{z}-1}\right|<1 \\
\Rightarrow|\mathrm{z}+1|<|\mathrm{z}-1| \\
\Rightarrow(\mathrm{x}+1)^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}<(\mathrm{x}-1)^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}<0
\end{array}$$

Set B
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \arg \left(\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{\mathrm{z}+1}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\
\Rightarrow \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}-1}\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}+1}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}+\frac{2 \mathrm{y}}{\sqrt{3}}-1=0
\end{array}$$
$A \cap B$
⇒ Centre $\left(0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

questions.text: Let A be a $3 \times 3$ invertible matrix. If $\mid$ adj $(24 \mathrm{~A}) \mid= \operatorname{adj}(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})) \mid$, then $|\mathrm{A}|^{2}$ is equal to :

options.D:
1

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $|\operatorname{adj}(24 \mathrm{~A})|=|\operatorname{adj} 3(\operatorname{adj} 2 \mathrm{~A})|$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow|24 \mathrm{a}|^{2}=(3 \operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A}))^{2} \\
\Rightarrow\left(24^{3} \mid \mathrm{Al}\right)^{2}=\left(3^{3}|\operatorname{adj}(2 \mathrm{~A})|\right)^{2} \\
=3^{6}\left(|2 \mathrm{~A}|^{2}\right)^{2} \\
\Rightarrow 24^{6}|\mathrm{~A}|^{2}=\left(24^{3}|\mathrm{~A}|\right)^{2}=3^{6} \times 2^{12}|\mathrm{~A}|^{4} \\
\Rightarrow|\mathrm{~A}|^{2}=\frac{24^{6}}{3^{6} \times 2^{12}}=64
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The remainder when $(2021)^{2023}$ is divided by 7 is :

options.D:
6

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $(2021)^{2023}=(7 \lambda-2)^{2023}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
={ }^{2023} \mathrm{C}_{0}(7 \mathrm{~A})^{2023}-\ldots \ldots{ }^{2023} \mathrm{C}_{2023} 2^{2023} \\
=7 \mathrm{t}-2^{2023} \\
\therefore-2^{2023}=-2 \times 2^{2022} \\
=-2 \times\left(2^{3}\right)^{674} \\
=-2(1+7 \mu)^{674} \\
=-(7 \alpha+2) \\
\Rightarrow \text { remainder }=-2 \text { or }+5
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{g}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be two real valued functions defined as $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}-|x+3| & , \quad x<0 \\ e^{x} & , \quad x \geq 0\end{array}\right.$ and $g(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}x^{2}+k_{1} x & , \quad x<0 \\ 4 x+k_{2} & , \quad x \geq 0\end{array}\right.$, where $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ are real constants. If (gof) is differentiable at $\mathrm{x}=0$, then (gof) (-4) + (gof) (4) is equal to :

options.D:
$2\left(2 \mathrm{e}^{4}-1\right)$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\left\{\begin{array}{lll}\mathrm{x}+3 & ; & \mathrm{x}<-3 \\ -(\mathrm{x}+3) & ; & -3 \leq \mathrm{x}<0 \\ \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}} & ; & \mathrm{x} \geq 0\end{array}\right\}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
g(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
x^{2}+k_{1} x & ; & x<0 \\
4 x+k_{2} & ; & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right\} \\
g(f(x))=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
f(x)^{2}+k_{1} f(x) & ; & f(x)<0 \\
4 f(x)+k_{2} & ; & f(x) \geq 0
\end{array}\right\} \\
g(f(x))=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
(x+3)^{2}+k_{1}(x+3) & ; & x<-3 \\
(x+3)^{2}-k_{1}(x+3) & ; & -3 \leq x<0 \\
4 e^{x}+k_{2} & ; & x>0
\end{array}\right\}
\end{array}$$
check continuity at $\mathrm{x}=0$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\operatorname{gof}(0)=g\left(f\left(0^{-}\right)\right)=g\left(f\left(0^{+}\right)\right) \\
4+k_{2}=9-3 k_{1}=4+k_{2} \\
3 k_{1}+k_{2}=5
\end{array}$$
differentiate
$$\begin{array}{l}
(\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})))^{\prime}=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
2(\mathrm{x}+3)+\mathrm{k}_{1} & ; & \mathrm{x}<-3 \\
2(\mathrm{x}+3)-\mathrm{k}_{1} & ; & -3 \leq \mathrm{x}<0 \\
4 \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}} & ; & \mathrm{x} \geq 0
\end{array}\right\} \\
6-\mathrm{k}_{1}=4 \\
\mathrm{k}_{1}=2 \\
\therefore \mathrm{k}_{1}=2, \mathrm{k}_{2}=-1
\end{array}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\operatorname{gof}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}
(x+3)^{2}+2(x+3) & ; & x<-3 \\
(x+3)^{2}-2(x+3) & ; & -3 \leq x<0 \\
4 e^{x}-1 & ; & x \geq 0
\end{array}\right\} \\
\operatorname{gof}(-4)+\operatorname{gof}(4)=4 e^{4}-2 \\
\Rightarrow 2\left(2 e^{4}-1\right)
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The sum of the absolute minimum and the absolute maximum values of the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\left|3 \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}^{2}+2\right|-\mathrm{x}$ in the interval $[-1,2]$ is :

options.D:
$\frac{9-\sqrt{17}}{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}x^{2}-4 x-2, & \forall x \in\left(-1, \frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}\right) \\ -x^{2}+2 x+2, & \forall x \in\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}, 2\right)\end{array}\right.$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ when $\mathrm{x} \in\left(-1, \frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}\right)$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2 \mathrm{x}-4=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=2$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2(\mathrm{x}-2) \quad \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ is always ↓
$f(2)=2$
$f(-1)=3$
$f\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2}$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ when $\mathrm{x} \in\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{17}}{2}, 2\right)$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-2 \mathrm{x}+2$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-2(\mathrm{x}-1)$
$f^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=0$ when $\mathrm{x}=1$
$f(1)=3$
absolute minimum value $=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2}$
absolute maximum value $=3$
$S u m=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2}+3=\frac{\sqrt{17}+3}{2}$

questions.text: Let S be the set of all the natural numbers, for which the line $\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{a}}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{b}}=2$ is a tangent to the curve $\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{a}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}+\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{b}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}=2$ at the point $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}), \mathrm{ab} \neq 0$. Then:

options.D:

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\left(\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{a}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}+\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{b}}\right)^{\mathrm{n}}=2$
Slope of tangent at (a, b)
$n \cdot\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^{n-1} \cdot \frac{1}{a}+n\left(\frac{x}{b}\right)^{n-1} \cdot \frac{1}{b} \frac{d y}{d x}=0$
$\left.\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right|_{(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b})}=-\frac{\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}$
∴ Equation of tangent
$\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{b}=-\frac{\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{a})$
$\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{a}}+\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{b}}=2 \forall \mathrm{n} \in \mathrm{N}$

questions.text: The area bounded by the curve $\mathrm{y}=\left|\mathrm{x}^{2}-9\right|$ and the line $\mathrm{y}=3$ is :

options.D:
$8(4 \sqrt{3}+\sqrt{6}-9)$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (Bonus)

Sol.

Area of shaded region
$$\begin{array}{l}
=2 \int_{0}^{3}(\sqrt{9+\mathrm{y}}-\sqrt{9-\mathrm{y}}) \mathrm{dy}+2 \int_{3}^{9}(\sqrt{9-\mathrm{y}}) \mathrm{dy} \\
=2\left[\int_{0}^{3}(9+\mathrm{y})^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dy}-\int_{0}^{3}(9-\mathrm{y})^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dy}+\int_{3}^{9}(9-\mathrm{y})^{1 / 2} \mathrm{dy}\right] \\
=2\left[\frac{2}{3}\left[(9+\mathrm{y})^{3 / 2}\right]_{0}^{3}+\frac{2}{3}\left[(9-\mathrm{y})^{3 / 2}\right]_{0}^{3}-\frac{2}{3}\left[(9-\mathrm{y})^{3 / 2}\right]_{3}^{9}\right] \\
=\frac{4}{3}[12 \sqrt{12}-27+6 \sqrt{6}-27-(0-6 \sqrt{6})] \\
=\frac{4}{3}[24 \sqrt{3}+12 \sqrt{6}-54] \\
=8(4 \sqrt{3}+2 \sqrt{6}-9)
\end{array}$$

$\frac{\mathrm{a}}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{b}}{5}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)

JEE Exam Solution

Sol. Let equation of rotated plane be :
$$\begin{array}{l}
(2 x+3 y+z+20)+\lambda(x-3 y+5 z-8)=0 \\
(2+\lambda) x+(3-3 \lambda) y+(1+5 \lambda) z+20-8 \lambda=0
\end{array}$$

Above plane is perpendicular to $2 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}+20=0$
So, $(2+\lambda) \cdot 2+(3-3 \lambda) \cdot 3+(1+5 \lambda) \cdot 1=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=7$
⇒ Equation of rotated plane : $\mathrm{x}-2 \mathrm{y}+4 \mathrm{z}-4=0$
Mirror image of $\mathrm{A}\left(2, \frac{-1}{2}, 2\right)$ in rotated plane is B(a, b, c)
Equation of $\mathrm{AB}: \frac{\mathrm{x}-2}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}+1 / 2}{-2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-2}{4}=\mathrm{k}$
Let coordinate of B be $\left(2+k, \frac{-1}{2}-2 k, 2+4 k\right)$ midpoint of AB is $\left(2+\frac{\mathrm{k}}{2}, \frac{-1}{2}-\mathrm{k}, 2+2 \mathrm{k}\right)$ which will lie on the plane $x-2 y+4 z-4=0$
Hence $\mathrm{k}=\frac{-2}{3}$
Therefore B is $\left(\frac{4}{3}, \frac{5}{6}, \frac{-2}{3}\right) \equiv\left(\frac{8}{6}, \frac{5}{6}, \frac{-4}{6}\right)$
So, $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{8}=\frac{\mathrm{b}}{5}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{-4}$

questions.text: Let a biased coin be tossed 5 times. If the probability of getting 4 heads is equal to the probability of getting 5 heads, then the probability of getting atmost two heads is:

options.D:
$\frac{46}{6^{4}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{H})=\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{T})=1-\mathrm{x}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{P}(4 \mathrm{H}, 1 \mathrm{~T})=\mathrm{P}(5 \mathrm{H}) \\
{ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{1}(\mathrm{x})^{4}(1-\mathrm{x})^{1}={ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{5} \mathrm{x}^{5} \\
5(1-\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x} \\
6 \mathrm{x}=5=0 \quad \mathrm{x}=\frac{5}{6}
\end{array}$$

P(atmost 2H)
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{OH}, 5 \mathrm{~T})+\mathrm{P}(1 \mathrm{H}, 4 \mathrm{~T})+\mathrm{P}(2 \mathrm{H}, 3 \mathrm{~T}) \\
={ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{0}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{5}+{ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{1} \frac{5}{6} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{4}+{ }^{5} \mathrm{C}_{2}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{3}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{3} \\
=\frac{1}{6^{5}}(1+25+250)=\frac{276}{6^{5}} \\
=\frac{46}{6^{4}}
\end{array}$$
